name: Lagoon Shore & Village Core
tagline: The palm-fringed heart of the oasis
description: The tight loop of restaurants, bars and shops ringing the small lagoon, where palms, still water and towering dunes meet. This is the postcard Huacachina, busiest at sunset and after dark, and everything here is walkable within a few minutes on foot.
cons: Very touristy and can feel crowded

name: Dune-Side Hostels
description: The cluster of hostels and guesthouses pressed against the dunes just back from the lagoon, home to the party scene, buggy pickups and rooftop sunset spots. It is where most backpackers sleep, socialise and launch their sandboarding runs into the surrounding desert.
pros: Easy access to buggy and sandboard tours
Rooftop sunset views over the dunes

name: Central Ica
description: A ten-minute taxi ride away, central Ica is the practical hub the oasis lacks, with supermarkets, banks, markets, more cafes and everyday services. Built around the Plaza de Armas, it is where you go for cheaper living, better connectivity and a genuine slice of city life.
cons: Requires a taxi to reach the dunes

name: Ica Winery & Pisco Road
description: The rural stretch outside Ica running past historic bodegas and vineyards such as Tacama and El Catador, where the region's pisco and wine are made. It offers tastings, tours and desert-vineyard scenery, an easy cultural half-day trip from the oasis.
